hypothesis: A clean FP32 CPU load and greedy-decoding inference run of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on this environment will produce memory and throughput figures of the same order of magnitude as the historical baseline (~8.23GB peak load RAM, ~6.71GB peak inference RAM, ~1.46 tok/s), despite differences in package versions and hardware allocation.

measurement.load_time_note: includes model download; NOT a warm-cache load-only measurement

result: Reproduced successfully. 12/12 prompts completed with no errors. Peak RAM during load: 8.6423 GB (historical: 8.23 GB). Peak RAM during inference: 6.9316 GB (historical: 6.71 GB). Average throughput: 1.3079 tok/s (historical: 1.46 tok/s). All figures are the same order of magnitude as the historical run; differences are attributable to transformers/accelerate version changes (5.17.0 vs unknown historical version) and explicit 2-thread pinning rather than implementation error.
conclusion: EXP-01 baseline is TRUSTWORTHY and REPRODUCIBLE under this environment (Python 3.13.15, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, 2 logical CPUs, 12.67GB RAM). This baseline — peak load ~8.6GB RAM, peak inference ~6.9GB RAM, ~1.3 tok/s, 12/12 success — is the reference point for all subsequent experiments (EXP-02 quantization onward). Per-prompt latency variance (8.4s–54.2s) was observed but not yet explained; flagged for monitoring, not blocking.
